summary.short: Sets application rules and exemption criteria under the Online News Act for digital news intermediary operators: an imbalance test with revenue and user thresholds, a 180-day notice duty to the Commission, and conditions for exemption orders. In force 19 December 2023.
summary.long: The Regulations, made under the Online News Act, do three things. First, for section 6 of the Act, they set when a significant bargaining power imbalance exists between an operator and news businesses: the operator's total revenue from all sources in the previous calendar year must exceed $1 billion, and the digital news intermediary must be a search engine with an average of at least 20 million unique visitors in Canada per month or a social media service with an average of at least 20 million active users in Canada per month. Second, an operator that must notify the Commission under subsection 7(1) of the Act must do so within 180 days after the Act begins to apply to the intermediary. Third, they set conditions for an exemption order under paragraph 11(1)(b) of the Act, including an open call process with notice periods of at least 60 days, information to the Commission, and a dollar valuation of non-monetary compensation. They also direct how the Commission interprets the compensation criteria: fair compensation, use of an appropriate portion for local, regional and national news content (a majority of monetary compensation), freedom and independence, and sustainability. For the largest search engine, a formula of $100 million adjusted by CPI applies. Group agreements are allowed, with allocation limits of 30% for non-CBC broadcasters and 7% for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. The text sets no penalties. It comes into force on December 19, 2023, or on registration if later.
